stages.title: You have been appointed Chancellor.
stages.doing: You are about to write a Budget: the taxes and the spending for the next few years.
stages.why: The [fiscal rules] limit how much you can borrow, and the [OBR](obr) checks your sums.
stages.now: Read what your three advisers have to tell you, then begin.

stages.title: Choose what to plan on
stages.doing: Pick the economic forecast you will build your Budget on, and how much [headroom] to keep in reserve.
stages.why: A rosier forecast gives you more to spend now. The [OBR](obr) will publish its own forecast later, and it will not care what you assumed.
stages.now: Choose one of the four cards and a headroom target, then confirm.

stages.title: Agree the themes with the Prime Minister
stages.doing: Tell the Prime Minister what this Budget is for, and pick the [flagship] schemes that will show it.
stages.why: Every flagship you tick is paid for at once, so your [headroom] falls as you choose. The [manifesto] red lines still apply.
stages.now: Tick the themes that apply, then the flagships you want. Watch the headroom.

stages.title: Build the package
stages.doing: Set taxes and spending across the whole of government, one folder at a time.
stages.why: This is where the money comes from and where it goes. A lever that breaks a [manifesto] promise shows a red warning.
stages.now: Open the tax folders and move what you want. Then the spending, then the policies.

stages.title: Build the package
stages.doing: Set taxes and spending across the whole of government, one folder at a time.
stages.why: This is where the money comes from and where it goes. A lever that breaks a [manifesto] promise shows a red warning.
stages.now: Set the departments, investment and welfare. Ministers will tell you what each change means.

stages.title: Build the package
stages.doing: Set taxes and spending across the whole of government, one folder at a time.
stages.why: This is where the money comes from and where it goes. A lever that breaks a [manifesto] promise shows a red warning.
stages.now: Adopt or refuse the policies your colleagues are campaigning for. Each one has a price.

stages.title: The OBR’s forecast arrives
stages.doing: The [OBR](obr) hands you the forecast your Budget will be judged against.
stages.why: It was fixed the day you chose your assumptions, and it may not match them. Your [headroom] can rise or fall.
stages.now: Open the envelope and see what it does to your plans.

stages.title: Make the sums add up
stages.doing: Close the gap between the [headroom] you have and the headroom you wanted.
stages.why: Every route costs something: more tax, less spending, a smaller promise, or a thinner safety margin.
stages.now: Take the routes you can live with, then move on to the speech.

stages.title: Something for the speech
stages.doing: Decide whether to add one surprise announcement, or to keep your [headroom].
stages.why: A rabbit gets the headlines. It is also money you no longer have in reserve.
stages.now: Pick a card. Keeping the headroom is a choice too.

stages.title: Deliver the Budget
stages.doing: Give the speech and see how your backbenchers, the markets and the public react.
stages.why: Each reaction follows from what you chose, and says which choices caused it.
stages.now: Read the speech, hear the reactions, then read the verdict.
